research_updates.title: Proposed expansion agreement expired
research_updates.notes: Hammond reports that the development agreement for 301 Digital Crossroads expired after its June 30, 2026 deadline. The city says it will offer no further extensions of that agreement. The 2025 proposed expansion and associated payment promises are not treated as active commitments or realized receipts. This update concerns the proposed expansion; it does not establish closure of the existing DX-1 facility.

source.title: Hammond Announces Expiration of Data Center Development Agreement
source.notes: Official city announcement retrieved as HTML. The proposed expansion agreement at 301 Digital Crossroads expired after unmet June 30, 2026 milestones and two extensions. This does not establish closure of the existing Digital Crossroad facility.

research_updates.title: Developer reports more than $80 million spent with local contractors
research_updates.notes: Official Council minutes record Decennial's co-founder describing more than $80 million spent with local contractors on the existing Building 1. The amount is a cumulative, developer-reported lower bound. Local geography, annual timing, contractor payments, worker counts, payroll and multiplier effects remain unverified.

source.title: Hammond Common Council Meeting Minutes — June 9, 2025
source.notes: The official minutes record a statement by Decennial Group co-founder David Pavlik during Council consideration of the later 301 Digital Crossroads proposal. He describes the existing Building 1, acquired mid-construction in 2021, and reports well over $80 million spent with local contractors for electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing, re-roofing and fiber work. The amount is developer testimony preserved in a public record, not an audited expenditure schedule. The minutes do not define local geography, spending start date, payroll, worker count, job-years or multiplier effects.

research_updates.title: Owner-funded improvement district separates estimates from City credit
research_updates.notes: Ordinance 9496 estimates Building 1 capital expenditure at $88,656,629 and creates potential owner special assessments for project debt and district expenses. The ordinance does not pledge City or state faith, credit or taxing power, and assigns excess zone expenses to the project owner. The application retains the cost and assessment caps as forecasts because no final EID bond, schedule, collection or expenditure was verified.

source.title: Hammond Ordinance 9496 — DX Hammond Economic Improvement District
source.notes: The enacted ordinance and attached petition establish a 67.52-acre economic improvement district for privately funded project debt. Exhibit J-1 gives an $88,656,629 Building 1 capital-cost estimate. Section 46 caps annual special assessments at $3,415,000 in Zone 1 and $3,415,000 in Zone 2, with Zone 3 exempt; assessments may remain for up to 25 years after an EID bond is issued. The ordinance says City, state and political-subdivision faith, credit and taxing power are not pledged to EID debt, and excess zone expenses are payable by the project owner. No EID bond issuance, final assessment schedule, collections or expenditures were verified in this review. The attached U.S. Chamber typical-data-center multipliers are contextual and are not encoded as Hammond facts.

research_updates.title: State debt register shows the existing TIF bond but no separate EID debt
research_updates.notes: Indiana Gateway's live Hammond Civil City outstanding-debt register includes the Series 2019 Data Center bond and no separately named DX Hammond Economic Improvement District or EID bond. This closes one public-record screen, not the entire financing question: a private obligation, unreported closing or separately administered instrument could fall outside the City register. EID bills, owner payments, district receipts and expenditures remain unverified.

source.title: Indiana Gateway Hammond Civil City Outstanding Bond/Lease Register
source.notes: The live Hammond Civil City outstanding-debt filter lists 33 debt names, including the existing City of Hammond Taxable Economic Development Revenue Bonds, Series 2019 (Data Center). It does not list a DX Hammond Economic Improvement District bond or another EID-labelled obligation. This is a bounded screen of Hammond Civil City's current self-reported debt register; it does not prove that no private obligation, unreported closing or separately administered instrument exists.

research_updates.title: Unsubmitted 2025 annual report blocks the debt-series extension
research_updates.notes: Gateway's rendered output states that Hammond Civil City has not yet submitted its 2025 Annual Financial Report. No apparent 2025 export value is admitted as an economic record. The audited Series 2019 principal, interest, pledged-revenue, transfer and remaining-commitment histories therefore stop at 2024 pending a submitted annual report or equivalent audited statement.

source.title: Indiana Gateway Hammond Civil City 2025 Debt Statement Report Status
source.notes: The rendered 2025 Debt Statement output states that Hammond Civil City has not yet submitted its 2025 Annual Financial Report. Apparent values exposed by a CSV export are therefore excluded. The application does not extend the audited Series 2019 balance, principal, interest, pledged-revenue, transfer or remaining-commitment series beyond 2024 from this source.

research_updates.title: Audited report separates operating scale, private financing and fund accounting
research_updates.notes: Principal reports year-end cost basis, fair value, 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned, 89.3% leased and occupied, and asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Cost basis, fair value and private debt remain separate stocks; neither debt-balance changes nor the report's fund-wide real-estate-improvements roll-forward are treated as Hammond annual capital spending. Utilization is not converted into MW, revenue, employment or measured electricity use.

source.title: Principal Digital Real Estate Fund (A), LP 2025 Annual Report — Audited Financial Statements
source.notes: Audited fund statements repeat the Hammond financing terms and report 2024-2025 project TIF revenues used toward loan repayments. The report states that these revenues were generated solely by real-estate tax payments made by Hammond Data Center. The audited consolidated schedule reports Hammond's 2024 and 2025 cost basis and fair value; the manager update reports 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned and 89.3% leased and occupied at year-end 2025. The debt note reports asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Its separate real-estate-improvements roll-forward covers the entire multi-property Aggregator and is not assigned to Hammond.

research_updates.notes: Lake County identifies the real-property account at 100 Digital Crossroads Drive as parcel 45-01-36-176-005.000-023 in the Hammond taxing unit. It covers the lease-area real property and remains separate from the personal-property value later collected from the city’s largest-taxpayer table.

research_updates.title: Audited fund statements confirm the TIF financing and repayment structure
research_updates.notes: The fund's audited statements confirm an $8.04 million City loan, its mirrored TIF bond and annual project TIF revenues applied to repayment. These amounts are presented as public-financing flows rather than a grant or general-fund revenue, and the annual repayments are not combined with gross parcel distributions.

source.title: Principal Digital Real Estate Fund 2023 Annual Report — Audited Financial Statements
source.notes: Audited fund statements describe the Hammond TIF bond and mirror loan, including the $8.04 million principal, 4% interest rate, 2044 maturity and 2022–2023 project TIF revenues applied to repayment. The arrangement is eliminated in the fund's consolidated statements.

research_updates.title: Development agreement adds a job forecast, local-labor requirements and water-permit limits
research_updates.notes: The agreement anticipated approximately 40 full-time jobs and required good-faith priority for Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractors and workers. Section 1.9(B)(2) also required the developer to retain relevant compliance data and provide it to the Redevelopment Commission at least quarterly until construction completion. The study treats the jobs as a forecast, the labor terms as requirements without realized participation data, and the water figures as permit capacities rather than use.

source.title: Development Agreement for Digital Crossroads of America Data Center and Technology Hub
source.notes: Executed development agreement attached to the city resolution. Section 1.9(B) requires good-faith priority for Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractors and workers, evidence about bids and awards, and quarterly compliance reporting to the Redevelopment Commission through construction completion. It also states prospective investment and job figures and water-permit capacities. The agreement does not itself report realized hiring, payroll, measured water use or confirmation that the permit transfer occurred.

research_updates.title: Contemporaneous completion report supplies a 17-employee operating snapshot
research_updates.notes: Data Center Dynamics reported 17 facility employees and separately described an expectation that customer staff could bring on-site employment to roughly 40. Only the 17-person snapshot is recorded as reported activity; the article's cooling description has no measured water volume.

source.title: Digital Crossroads finishes $40m Lake Michigan data center in Indiana
source.notes: Contemporaneous trade-press completion report states that the operating facility employed 17 people and describes Lake Michigan water cooling. The employee figure is a facility snapshot, not a payroll record, annual average or local-residency count; the cooling description includes no measured water volume.

research_updates.title: City audit establishes the data-center bond's pre-amortization baseline
research_updates.notes: At year-end 2022 the City reported $8.04 million of outstanding Series 2019 principal, no principal retired, $321,600 of interest and fees and $12,074,400 of future principal-plus-interest commitment. Pledged TIF revenue, the debt-service-fund transfer and the private fund's loan-repayment amount retain their separate labels.

research_updates.title: Audited principal amortization begins in 2023
research_updates.notes: The Series 2019 Data Center fund retired $65,000 of principal and reported $321,600 of interest and fees in 2023, leaving $7.975 million outstanding. Repeated balances are not annual flows, and the reports do not disclose transaction dates or establish realized EDGE employment.

research_updates.title: Quarterly local-labor records have a defined acquisition path
research_updates.notes: The 2018 agreement required quarterly reporting to the Redevelopment Commission on compliance with its Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractor and worker priorities. No named filing was located in the City’s indexed public document archive, whose Redevelopment Commission categories begin in 2021. This is an unresolved already-public evidence gap, not evidence of noncompliance or zero local participation. No public-records request or other solicitation is recommended.

economic_sources.title: Hammond Ordinance 9496 — DX Hammond Economic Improvement District
economic_sources.notes: The enacted ordinance and attached petition establish a 67.52-acre economic improvement district for privately funded project debt. Exhibit J-1 gives an $88,656,629 Building 1 capital-cost estimate. Section 46 caps annual special assessments at $3,415,000 in Zone 1 and $3,415,000 in Zone 2, with Zone 3 exempt; assessments may remain for up to 25 years after an EID bond is issued. The ordinance says City, state and political-subdivision faith, credit and taxing power are not pledged to EID debt, and excess zone expenses are payable by the project owner. No EID bond issuance, final assessment schedule, collections or expenditures were verified in this review. The attached U.S. Chamber typical-data-center multipliers are contextual and are not encoded as Hammond facts.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project.
